did_you_know.text: In Jewish tradition, “I am” is counted as the first commandment. It begins by presenting the relationship between God and the people, rather than with an order.
The phrase “to carry the name” does not mean physically carrying it; it refers to using the name in speech or an oath. The verse therefore warns against using God’s name falsely or carelessly.
The Hebrew word Shabbat is related to the root meaning “to stop” or “to cease.” It therefore describes not only a day on the calendar, but also a pause from work.
Sabbath rest is meant for everyone in the household, including servants, resident foreigners, and animals. It is presented as a time of rest not limited to people of high status.

The verse says “You shall not murder,” not simply “You shall not kill.” In biblical Hebrew, the verb generally refers to unlawful or criminal killing, which is why many translations use the word “murder.”
The phrase “they saw the sounds” combines sight and hearing. It creates an image of an experience so powerful that all the senses seem to take part in it.
The altar is to be made of whole stones, without shaping them with a sword or an iron tool. The verse connects a sacred place with avoiding the symbolism of weapons.
